clue.text: The liveliness of Paris, say, after examination

indicators.note: after places the city piece behind the examination piece in the answer

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination at a university
Paris is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Someone describes the buzz of the French capital once their exams are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris, say' looks like a French reference but is just an example of a city. A viva (viva voce) is the spoken exam a student may face at a British university.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivacity is spirited energy, a synonym for liveliness.

clue.text: Personal concern for private gain involving half cover?

explanation.surface: A self-serving motive is described, with a coy aside about a garment covering only part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a joke: a vest covers only the top half of the body, so something to do with a vest might be called vested.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish stake someone holds in an outcome is the idiom; jokingly, a concern with a vest, which covers the upper body only.

clue.text: Thing in navy involved a lot of pride

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other piece
involved means tangled up, so the letters of navy are mixed

parts.note: it is a common stand-in word for a thing

explanation.surface: Something aboard a warship turns out to be mostly about conceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles the ship word and 'in' sets the stand-in for 'Thing' within that scramble, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity is excessive pride in oneself, a near synonym.

clue.text: Open vault

explanation.surface: A two-word note that reads like an instruction about a bank strongroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear means free of obstruction or unobstructed; it also means to jump over a fence or bar, as a pole-vaulter does.

clue.text: It requires keyboard skills of touch and technique

definitions.text: It requires keyboard skills of touch and technique

parts.words: It requires keyboard skills of touch and technique
parts.note: a showy piece for organ or harpsichord whose name comes from the Italian verb meaning to touch

explanation.surface: A remark about the dexterity needed to play a demanding piece at the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition meant to display a player's touch and fingerwork.

clue.text: The plant that has an account with a US agency

parts.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for an account
the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A shrub apparently banks with an American spy outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: AC (as in A/C) for account comes first, then A and CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of tree or shrub, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Miserable supporters will

parts.note: the clue is an unfinished sentence that the answer completes: gloomy fans will make less noise for their side

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction about a team's fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer finishes the clue's sentence; read whole, it means miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless means dreary and joyless, close in sense to miserable.

clue.text: Vehicle with a speed topping a tortoise, say!

parts.note: a car is a common vehicle
pace means speed or rate of movement

explanation.surface: A fast car racing a tortoise, which would be a mismatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' is a noun here: the thing that sits on top of a tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle or tortoise, covering its back.

clue.text: One ill (chest) and dodgy fibrous cord in leg

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or unsound, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient with a bad chest also has a dodgy leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges the fourteen letters of ONE ILL CHEST AND.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the band of tissue joining the calf muscle to the heel bone, a fibrous cord in the lower leg.

clue.text: A number of words in judgment?

explanation.surface: Someone muses on how many words go into a court ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit made of several words; also the punishment a judge hands down.

clue.text: The art house shows a symbol of home

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display inside the words the art house

explanation.surface: An arts cinema is putting on a film about domestic life.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'tHE ART House'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside is a traditional emblem of family life and domestic comfort.

clue.text: Difficult problem resulting from a tie

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arising from a match ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangled puzzle or snag; also a fastening made by tying rope or string.

clue.text: Train teen unusually to be host

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so these letters come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Coaching a teenager to receive guests in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges TRAIN TEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is to receive and feed guests, which is what a host does.

clue.text: Outcast returning to produce feeling of distaste

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for an outcast is read backwards

parts.note: a leper is a person shunned by society

explanation.surface: A shunned person comes back and provokes disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LEPER back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel can mean to disgust or cause aversion in someone.

clue.text: In favour of a number of meetings for discussion

parts.note: for means supporting or in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone supports holding a series of debating sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural, so the Latin plural of forum is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Forums are public gatherings for debate, and the Latin plural form is used here.

clue.text: A painting for the teacher about to retire?

explanation.surface: A gift picture chosen for a schoolmaster's leaving do.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas by a great European artist before about 1800; jokingly, an aged schoolmaster ready for retirement.

clue.text: The blandishments of Lear etc in a new version

indicators.note: a new version of something is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds a fresh production of King Lear overly sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a new version' rearranges LEAR ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively it is cloying, flattering talk or sentiment, like blandishments.

clue.text: See 1
Affirm lease in small political power region

parts.note: to state is to declare or affirm
to let is to lease a property

explanation.surface: A landlord confirms a rental agreement in a tiny country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A statelet is a small state, a minor political territory.

clue.text: Observed leap year initially in a distinguished way

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the words leap and year

explanation.surface: Someone spotted that it was a leap year and acted with style.
explanation.definitionFit: Notedly means in an eminent or famous manner.

clue.text: A meditation from Goya possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the painter's name may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A contemplative scene perhaps painted by the Spanish artist Goya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GOYA.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a discipline of breathing and posture used as a form of meditation.

clue.text: A flower? This provides a spray!

explanation.surface: A florist's quip that a single bloom can make a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: A spray is also a small bunch of flowers, which misleads; the second sense is the perforated nozzle on a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: A common garden bloom; also the perforated sprinkler head fitted to a watering can or hose.

clue.text: Old Testament proof put out one of the high-ups

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Bible scholar's evidence is thrown into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges OT and PROOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftop is one of the highest points of a building, so is jokingly a high-up.

clue.text: Hint given with no thanks coining up eventually

indicators.note: with no means the following piece is taken out of the hint word

parts.note: to intimate is to hint at something

indicators.note: coining is a scan misreading of coming; in a down clue coming up means the word for thanks is read upwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A suggestion offered ungratefully will be acted on sooner or later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coining' is an OCR slip for 'coming'. 'coming up' turns TA into AT, and 'with no' takes AT out of INTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: In time means sooner or later, an idiom for eventually.

clue.text: See 8
Additional term of cricket

explanation.surface: A note that something extra is a sporting word.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the British bat-and-ball game; such runs are added to the team total without credit to a batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than usual; in cricket it is a run scored other than off the bat, such as a wide or no-ball.

clue.text: See dons go for special training showing soundness of judgment

indicators.note: training puts things through a drill, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: University teachers are sent on a course to improve their decision-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for special training' rearranges SEE DONS GO. Dons are university lecturers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Good sense is sound practical judgment, the same as soundness of judgment.

clue.text: Bay hedge

explanation.surface: Two words that suggest a coastline and a garden boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A stall is a compartment in a stable or a bay; to stall is also to be evasive or hedge.

clue.text: Crude oil found during the drilling in Flint

indicators.note: found during means one piece is placed within the other
drilling puts troops through manoeuvres, so these letters change position
crude means unrefined or rough, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Petroleum is struck while boring into rock in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' and 'drilling' each scramble a short word, and 'found during' sets one inside the other. Flint is also a town in north Wales, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An eolith is a crudely chipped flint stone once thought to be an early human tool.

clue.text: Seat collapsed, went west. Needed to be this?

indicators.note: collapsed means fell apart, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: to go west is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A chair gave way and the sitter died, which shows it should have been propped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges SEAT to STEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Read back, the seat needed to be made firm and stable, which is to have been steadied.

clue.text: Tree from afar — at Otago, perhaps, being recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the run is read backwards
from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tree perhaps remembered from a distant New Zealand region.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'afAR AT OTago' read backwards gives the answer. Otago is a region of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The totara is a New Zealand conifer valued for its timber.

clue.text: Rascal from Ireland upset p-pals (even literally)

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: in literary or poetic writing even is contracted to e'en

explanation.surface: Stammered friends from Ireland are upset by a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges PPALS to SPALP; EEN is the poetic contraction e'en.
explanation.definitionFit: A spalpeen is an Irish word for a scamp or good-for-nothing.
